extracted.intended_audience: Wolfram Language / Wolfram System notebook users (programmers, students, educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using Wolfram System notebooks: how to enter and run input, organize cells and groups, format content, operate graphics, customize the environment, and perform global notebook operations for interactive computation and publishable documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebook purpose and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: From simple calculations to full publishable documents and sophisticated dynamic interfaces, everything you can do with the Wolfram System's standard interactive interface is done in a notebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notebooks are computational documents that support live computation, arbitrary dynamic interfaces, full typeset input, image input, automatic code annotation, a complete high-level programmatic interface, and thousands of functions and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to do a computation / run input
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the notebook interface to enter input and evaluate; choose appropriate execution commands and be aware of how to start input (e.g., special leading characters or entry modes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Input method selection
rubrics_metrics.description: choose how to enter input (Wolfram Language, free-form, text, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can enter pure Wolfram Language code, free-form linguistic queries, or plain text; pick the input mode that matches the task and ensures correct parsing and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-form linguistics input
rubrics_metrics.description: use free-form linguistics to generate Wolfram System output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free-form input lets you type natural-language queries which the system interprets to produce Wolfram Language output; use this for exploratory queries or when concise natural phrasing is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting information, help, and context menus
rubrics_metrics.description: get information or help; right-click — get a context-specific menu
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contextual help and right-click menus for quick access to relevant operations, documentation, and shortcuts tailored to the selected cell or object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell groups and outlining operations
rubrics_metrics.description: double-click a group bracket — open or close a cell group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage notebook structure with cell groups and outlining; double-click group brackets to expand/collapse groups for navigation and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell bracket operations
rubrics_metrics.description: double-click cell brackets — close all other cells in a group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cell-bracket double-clicks to focus on a single cell while collapsing others in the same group; helpful for editing or hiding ancillary content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing computations
rubrics_metrics.description: abort a computation; copy input from above
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control running evaluations (abort long-running processes) and reuse previous inputs by copying them from earlier cells to avoid retyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting and typing shortcuts
rubrics_metrics.description: triple-click — select a function and its arguments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use selection shortcuts (triple-click, etc.) for quick selection of expressions; employ subscript and special-character input methods and convert forms (e.g., Convert to StandardForm) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and typesetting considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscript ( ) ▪ Special Character ▪ Convert to StandardForm ▪ Why the Coloring?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use built-in special-character handling and typesetting features for mathematical notation; be aware of cell formatting (StandardForm vs. TraditionalForm) and syntax coloring that indicate structure and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Styling and formatting cells
rubrics_metrics.description: text cell (with default stylesheet) (Format ▶ Style ▶ ...); section-heading cell (with default stylesheet); create a new cell of the same style (Format ▶ Stylesheet ▪ ...)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply cell styles for document structure and consistent appearance; use stylesheets and the Format menu to create or modify styles for text, headings, and code cells to produce publishable documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics operations
rubrics_metrics.description: drag — rotate a 3D graphic; toggle canvas (Graphics ▶ Convert To/From Canvas)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interact with graphics directly (drag to rotate 3D objects) and use canvas conversion to enable drawing or editing operations on graphic objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global notebook operations (file/export/history/spellcheck/send)
rubrics_metrics.description: Save As ▶ HTML, etc.; Notebook History; Check Spelling; Send To
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use File / Save As to export notebooks in different formats (HTML and others), review notebook history for changes, run spell-checking for prose, and use Send To for sharing or publishing workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebook environment customization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize the notebook environment through Preferences and the Option Inspector to set global behaviors, default styles, evaluation settings, and interface options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Menu-driven operations and insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: File ▶ New ▪ Save ▪ Print ▪ Exit ...; Insert ▶ Table/Matrix ▪ New Canvas ▪ Option Inspector ▪ ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize with menu items for document creation, saving, printing, inserting structured content (tables, matrices), and invoking tools (Option Inspector) to streamline notebook authoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and international character support
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Guides: Accessibility; International Character Sets; Special Characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the accessibility features and international character-set support to make notebooks usable by a broader audience and correctly render non-ASCII input and special symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebooks as expressions and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Notebooks as Wolfram Language Expressions; Notebooks as Documents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that notebooks are both programmatic Wolfram Language expressions (manipulable by code) and human-readable documents suitable for publishing; leverage both aspects for reproducibility and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related resources and learning pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Links: Wolfram U — Introduction to Notebooks; Introductory Book; Wolfram Function Repository; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult linked tutorials, courses, repositories, and tech notes for deeper learning, examples, and community resources to improve notebook design and usage.
